text.scope: Published texts on six propositions about AI and biology (P1 to P6): papers and their abstracts, perspectives, journal news articles, company announcements and press releases. Developer model papers are the subject of the `models` pass and company statements of the `companies` pass; this pass records only their stance on a proposition. Biosecurity propositions are left to the ai-bio-pack.
routes: Europe PMC REST search (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=…&format=json), lite results sorted by publication date ascending, then core records (resultType=core) for abstracts and dates; Europe PMC full-text XML (/PMC…/fullTextXML) where open
Article pages on nature.com (Nature, Nature Methods, Nature Medicine, Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Scientific Reports), retrieved directly
arXiv abstract pages (arxiv.org/abs/…v1) and the bioRxiv details API (api.biorxiv.org/details/biorxiv/<doi>)
Company sites retrieved directly: deepmind.google, isomorphiclabs.com (news listing and articles), evolutionaryscale.ai, sumitomo-pharma.com, insilico.com (news listing, to locate release addresses)
Internet Archive availability API for one capture (deepmind.com, December 2020)

Candidate lookup by title or DOI: several texts (Wong et al. 2022, Terwilliger et al. 2023, Lyu et al. 2024, Ma et al. 2018, Ahlmann-Eltze et al. 2025, Jayatunga et al. 2024, Xu et al. 2025, Huang et al. 2016, Anishchenko et al. 2020/2021, Watson et al. 2023, Bunne et al. 2024) were looked up as candidates by title or DOI rather than found by the term searches below; every record rests on the text then retrieved. Such lookups find what is already known and bias the earliest-located roles toward well-cited texts.

termsAndYears.P1: Europe PMC: TITLE_ABS "structure prediction" AND "drug design", 1970–1995 (3 hits); ABSTRACT "structure prediction" AND drug, 1970–1994 (2 hits); TITLE "prediction of protein structures", 1970–1990 (2 hits); abstract phrases "predicted structure", "structure prediction", "predicting the structure", "tertiary structure" with "drug design" or "design of drugs", 1960–1987 (0 hits, which shows phrase matching is exact and that Blundell et al. 1987 was found only through the title search); TITLE AlphaFold AND "drug discovery", 2020–2023 (6 hits). DeepMind's 2020 account was read because the dataset already holds it.
termsAndYears.P2: Europe PMC: TITLE_ABS "virtual cell", 1960–2001 (18 hits; the earliest is a 1993 Trends in Genetics title by Casini with no abstract, not read); "virtual cell" with machine learning, deep learning, artificial intelligence or neural network, to 2021 (2 hits, neither on the criterion); "virtual cell", "whole-cell model", "model of a cell" or "simulate cell" with deep learning, neural network or artificial intelligence, MEDLINE, 1990–2023 (43 hits, none earlier than Ma et al. 2018 on the criterion); TITLE "virtual cell challenge" (3 hits). The combined search did not return Ma et al. 2018, which was looked up by its title as a candidate and then retrieved; searches for "in silico cell" and "cell simulation" with machine learning were not run, so the P2 earliest-located role is weakly bounded.
termsAndYears.P3: No bibliographic search was run for company statements: the Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma and Exscientia release of January 2020 and Insilico Medicine's statements were located from the companies' own newsrooms. Earlier company statements that a named AI-discovered candidate began a trial (for example from companies founded before 2015) were not searched; press-release archives (Business Wire, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire) were not searched systematically, and GlobeNewswire refused the one release tried.
termsAndYears.P4: Europe PMC: TITLE_ABS "protein design" with neural network, machine learning, deep learning or artificial intelligence, to 2018 (39 hits, mostly stability prediction and engineering of natural proteins, none meeting the criterion); TITLE "protein design" with deep, neural, machine learning or generative, 2015–2020 (9 hits). The earliest located (Anishchenko et al., bioRxiv v1 of 23 July 2020) is bounded: preprints on generative models for protein design from 2019 (gcWGAN, autoregressive generative models; Europe PMC preprint records) were listed but not read, and could meet the criterion.
termsAndYears.P5: Europe PMC: abstract phrases "biology is an informational science", "biology has become an information science", "biology is an information science" (12 hits; Hood and Galas 2003 read). No search was run for "programmable biology", "digital biology" or "language of life" with machine learning, and no book or lecture literature was searched; the earliest located (Isomorphic Labs, 2021) is weakly bounded.
termsAndYears.P6: Located through the companies and trial texts above (Jayatunga et al. 2024 by title search in Europe PMC). No systematic search for analyses of AI-discovered drug success rates was run; later analyses (2025–2026) may exist.

gaps: Paywalled article bodies were not read: Nature (1987, 2003, 2016), Nature Methods (2018) and the Nature and Nature Reviews Drug Discovery news articles were read in their abstracts or standfirsts only. Five texts (Sternberg 1992, Tomita 2001, Lyu 2024, Jayatunga 2024, Roohani 2025) were read only in Europe PMC records of their abstracts.

science.org was not tried (refused per the brief); the PMC page for Lyu et al. returned a browser check and the Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500; the Elsevier page for Jayatunga et al. returned no readable text; cell.com was not tried.

Europe PMC abstract coverage before the mid-1970s is thin, so P1 and P2 searches cannot show earlier texts; no book, conference proceedings (for example ISMB, Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing) or pre-1987 review literature was searched.
No non-English text was searched; Chinese-language texts on these propositions (for example from BioMap or XtalPi) were not looked for.
Interviews, talks, op-eds and general press were not searched; DeepMind's and Isomorphic Labs' other posts were listed but only the two recorded were read.

The pages of DeepMind (2020), Isomorphic Labs (2021) and EvolutionaryScale (2024) were read as served on 2026-10-30; their wording is attested from that date. The December 2020 Internet Archive capture of DeepMind's account returned HTTP 403.

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: Biological design tools pose risks distinct from those of language models
biosecurityLinks.why: The sibling pack's proposition B4: AI tools built to design or predict biological molecules or systems pose misuse risks distinct from language models. The models recorded in this pack (structure prediction, protein design, protein and genomic language models) are the kind of tool the proposition is about; this pack records no position on it.

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: Sandbrink's preprint (arXiv v1, 24 June 2023) differentiates large language models from biological design tools, stating that language models in particular lower barriers to biological misuse while design tools expand the capabilities of sophisticated actors.
biosecurityLinks.why: A text that articulates B4 (Sandbrink, arXiv v1, 24 June 2023).

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: The preprint "Towards Responsible Governance of Biological Design Tools" (arXiv v1, 27 November 2023) states that biological design tools pose distinct regulatory challenges and that regulatory proposals tailored to large language models may be less effective for them.
biosecurityLinks.why: A text that articulates B4 (preprint of 27 November 2023 on governance of biological design tools).

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: CSET's explainer of December 2023 treats biological design tools as a separate class from chatbots, stating that their use in its current state requires both scientific and programming expertise.
biosecurityLinks.why: A text that articulates B4 (CSET explainer, December 2023).

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: Sandbrink's preprint (arXiv v1, 24 June 2023) states that biological design tools will expand the capabilities of sophisticated actors, and proposes interventions to deter biological misuse by such actors.
biosecurityLinks.why: Sandbrink's statement that biological design tools will expand the capabilities of sophisticated actors (proposition B7).

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: Synthesis-order screening is a control point for AI-related biological risk
biosecurityLinks.why: The sibling pack's proposition B5 on synthesis-order screening as a control point.

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: The preprint of 27 November 2023 states that the design capabilities of biological design tools could be used to evade DNA screening techniques, against the premise that screening at synthesis is a dependable control point.
biosecurityLinks.why: A text that contests B5 on the ground that design tools could be used to evade screening; recorded at policy level in the sibling pack.

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: Public release of model weights increases biological misuse risk
biosecurityLinks.why: The sibling pack's proposition B6 on public release of model weights; several models in this pack were released with weights, as their papers or developers state.

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: The preprint of 27 November 2023 identifies, among the challenges of regulating biological design tools, the potential for safeguards to be circumvented by open-sourcing model weights.
biosecurityLinks.why: A text that names open-sourcing of model weights among the challenges of regulating biological design tools (B6).

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: Working paper BWC/MSP/2025/WP.4, submitted by the United Kingdom to the 2025 Meeting of States Parties, states in its fifty-year timeline of life-science advances that the AlphaFold protein-folding prediction database published by DeepMind in 2021 accelerated scientific research in fields such as drug discovery but also demonstrated potential for misuse, highlighting the importance of stronger guard rails and AI governance.
biosecurityLinks.why: A UK working paper to the 2025 Meeting of States Parties of the Biological Weapons Convention that names AlphaFold in its timeline of life-science advances.

biosecurityLinks.siblingText: The UK screening guidance states that increased access to synthetic nucleic acids, coupled with developments in converging tools and technologies such as AI and an increase in knowledge and expertise, may exacerbate the risks of engineering biology.
biosecurityLinks.why: The UK synthetic nucleic acid screening guidance (October 2024) names AI among converging tools and technologies in its background statement.
